facts.text: Victoria–Fraserview began as one of the earliest settlement areas, with first European settlers arriving in the 1860s and a wagon road built in 1875.
The neighbourhood sits on a south‑facing slope overlooking the Fraser River, Mitchell Island, Richmond and Delta.
In the 1940s, 1,100 new homes were built for World War II veterans on land expropriated by the CMHC, sparking a rapid post‑war expansion.
The Fraserview branch of Vancouver Public Library on Argyle Drive serves the community and is within walking distance of David Thompson Secondary School.
The Avalon Dairy remains the only heritage building in Victoria–Fraserview, a relic of the neighbourhood’s early industrial past.
The Fraserlands development has turned former industrial riverfront into condominiums and other residential projects, reshaping the area since the 1980s.
